title: Streaming: typed disconnect errors w/ request_id + partial output semantics
author: Sabrina James
description:
Context
We have multiple reports of streaming requests terminating mid-response (corp proxies, flaky networks, server FIN mid-chunk). Today the iterator tends to surface a generic httpx/requests exception (or StopIteration) without (a) request_id, (b) a typed error class to allow customer handling, or (c) any access to partial output that was already received. This is also blocking cross-language parity work where TS/Go are converging on explicit disconnect taxonomy.

What this PR does
- Introduces a typed exception for streaming disconnects: StreamDisconnectedError (subclass of RedwoodAPIError) that carries request_id, status_code (when known), retryable flag, and partial_response (accumulated text + token/event counts).
- Makes streaming partial output semantics explicit:
  - The streaming iterator yields events as they arrive.
  - If the underlying connection terminates unexpectedly after at least one event has been yielded, we raise StreamDisconnectedError.
  - The exception includes partial_response so callers can decide whether to keep partial output, show it with a warning, or attempt a new request.
  - We do NOT auto-retry streaming (by design) to avoid duplicating side effects / billing ambiguity.
- Improves request_id capture and propagation:
  - Prefer x-redwood-request-id (and x-request-id fallback) from the initial response headers.
  - If headers are unavailable (some proxy modes), attempt to parse request_id from the first SSE event metadata when present.
  - Ensure StreamDisconnectedError.request_id is populated whenever we can recover it.
- Documents retry guidance for streaming in the Python README + docstrings:
  - Safe retry only before any tokens/events were received.
  - After first token, retry is application-dependent; recommend idempotency keys where applicable and logging request_id.
- Adds tests for mid-stream disconnects + proxy-buffered disconnect behavior using a deterministic streaming test server and a socket-level “cut connection mid-event” helper.

Why this aligns with the SDK parity standard
- Error taxonomy: provides typed error with request_id and retryable signal.
- Streaming semantics: consistent with conservative retry stance agreed in parity RFC (no implicit retries for streaming; surface partial output + guidance).

Implementation notes
- Added redwood.errors.StreamDisconnectedError + StreamingPartialResponse dataclass.
- Updated ChatCompletionStream (and legacy generate_stream) to accumulate partial text and event_count.
- Normalizes low-level exceptions (httpx.ReadError, httpcore.RemoteProtocolError, requests.exceptions.ChunkedEncodingError) into StreamDisconnectedError when they occur after streaming has started.
- Handles the “disconnect before first event” case as a regular transport error (still retryable via non-streaming retry middleware if enabled).

Backward compatibility
- No changes to successful streaming output.
- Behavior change: instead of occasionally returning silently / raising a generic network exception, callers will now reliably receive StreamDisconnectedError for mid-stream termination. This is intentionally more actionable.

Screenshots / examples
Python example:
try:
    stream = client.chat.completions.stream(model="redwood/verified-7b", messages=[...])
    for event in stream:
        ...
except StreamDisconnectedError as e:
    logger.warning("stream disconnected", extra={"request_id": e.request_id, "partial_len": len(e.partial_response.text), "events": e.partial_response.event_count})
    # retry guidance: only retry automatically if e.partial_response.event_count == 0

Testing
- Added unit tests for:
  - disconnect after N events -> raises StreamDisconnectedError w/ partial_response
  - disconnect before first event -> bubbles as transport error (retryable via normal policy)
  - request_id extraction from headers
  - request_id extraction from SSE metadata fallback
  - error redaction: ensure API key never appears in exception repr

Release note
Python SDK streaming now raises StreamDisconnectedError (includes request_id + partial output) when a stream terminates unexpectedly. Streaming is not automatically retried; docs include recommended retry patterns.
commits: streaming: accumulate partial text + event_count; normalize disconnect exceptions
streaming: request_id extraction from headers + SSE fallback
docs: add streaming retry guidance + partial output semantics
review_conversation: Ibrahim Khan (review): Can we make the retry guidance explicit in the exception itself (retryable flag semantics)? Specifically: retryable=true if we never emitted an event, otherwise false. Also, please make sure request_id is pulled from x-redwood-request-id first (parity standard).

Sabrina James (author): Updated. StreamDisconnectedError.retryable is now computed based on whether any streaming events were yielded. Also adjusted request id precedence: x-redwood-request-id -> x-request-id -> SSE metadata fallback. Added tests.

Allison Grant (review): Please ensure we capture enough fields for debugging/telemetry: request_id, disconnect_reason (best-effort), retry_count (should be 0 for streaming), timeout_ms (if available). Even if we can’t emit telemetry yet, the error should expose these. Also check that repr/str does not include raw headers.

Sabrina James (author): Added disconnect_reason (enum-ish string: remote_closed|protocol_error|read_timeout|unknown) and set retry_count=0 for StreamDisconnectedError. Timeout_ms is plumbed when the underlying client provides it (httpx timeout config). Confirmed error string does not log headers; tests added for redaction.
Owen Phillips (review): This resolves SUP-29410? The customer repro was “timeout ignored while streaming” and then a hard hang. Do we now reliably cancel/raise when read timeout is hit?

Sabrina James (author): Yes—read timeouts now map to StreamDisconnectedError(disconnect_reason=read_timeout) once streaming has started; prior behavior sometimes bubbled as httpx.ReadTimeout without request_id. For the hang case, the iterator now checks for keepalive timeouts and raises after the configured read timeout. Added fixture that simulates proxy buffering to confirm we don’t spin indefinitely.
Dana Lo (review): TS/Go are using partial_output fields named partial_text and event_count. Any chance we match names to keep parity docs simpler?

Sabrina James (author): Kept Python idioms but aligned field names in the public surface: partial_response.text + partial_response.event_count. Docs now show the equivalent names per language; we can revisit if we want strict naming parity at the exception field level.
release_notes: Streaming: raise StreamDisconnectedError on mid-stream termination (includes request_id, disconnect_reason, and partial_response).
Docs: clarify that streaming is not auto-retried; provide safe retry guidance (only auto-retry before first event).
